core_concepts: Questions
The book begins by arguing that experiments fail early when the question is vague
Decision linkage
The chapter says every experiment should answer a downstream decision
Mechanism before metric
The author also insists on mechanism before metric
Questions The book begins by arguing that experiments fail early when the question is vague
A useful question names the decision it is meant to improve, the behavior it is expected to change, and the mechanism that supposedly links the intervention to the outcome
If no decision changes when the result arrives, the project is probably collecting trivia rather than evidence
This does not mean exploratory work is useless
It means exploratory work should be labeled honestly and judged by whether it generates sharper later questions
That order is backwards
Measures
The chapter on measurement explains that metrics are not neutral windows onto reality
Good measure design
A good measure is relevant, sensitive enough to move when the underlying process changes, and stable enough that noise does not overwhelm the signal
Common trap
A common trap is choosing a metric that is easy to collect but weakly connected to the real objective

Good measure design A good measure is relevant, sensitive enough to move when the underlying process changes, and stable enough that noise does not overwhelm the signal

The final chapter argues that good interpretation compares the observed result with the pre-registered expectation, the measurement process, and plausible alternative explanations
If the team only records the primary metric, they may celebrate the improvement while misunderstanding the causal path that produced it
If two explanations remain plausible, the team should say so and design a follow-up test
